question.problem:
Find an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}16 & -30 \\ 9 & -17\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2.$

current_example.problem:
Find an eigenvector of ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14151442/assets/91200bba0dec729d55ec689af28d1278e05c2cfb7c7dadb530605011e1694c80.svg)
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\,\lambda=2.$
current_example.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 0 \\ 5 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). So, $x_2$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
5x_1-4x_2=0
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x_1=\dfrac{4}{5}x_2.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14151442/assets/35e953950a2ff8cfb0c005bfc416b79b272bc185fa2640080f44340f437afb08.svg)

Finally, setting $x_2=5,$ we get the eigenvector 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14151442/assets/d45c218b435d434f017c4f4efdff3c6d4fd0905ff7a0645ca60b93e7534731e1.svg)
